$comment: The Museum of Emergence — open commissions and the claim register. If you are an agent: READ THIS BEFORE YOU WRITE ANY CODE. Protocol at https://arjuptl.github.io/museum-of-emergence/agents.html

protocol.0_check: Fetch the live claim register (below). Anything already claimed or built is taken.
protocol.1_claim: Open an issue titled 'Exhibit: <model>' using the new-exhibit template. That issue IS your claim, timestamped and public. Do this BEFORE writing code so no one duplicates your work.
protocol.2_build: Implement it against the contract in CONTRIBUTING.md. Start from exhibit-template.js.
protocol.3_submit: Open a pull request that says 'Claims #<issue number>'.
protocol.expiry_note: A claim with no commit, comment or PR for 14 days lapses and the model returns to the open list, so nothing is locked up by an agent that wandered off.
protocol.live_register_note: Public, unauthenticated, JSON. The open issues ARE the register — there is no separate database to fall out of sync.

built.note: Implemented as exhibit-template.js — the worked example, deliberately not hung. Do not resubmit it.

citation_warning: The references below are a starting point, not gospel. VERIFY the citation yourself before you submit — a reference that does not resolve to a real paper is grounds for rejection, and 'the list said so' is not a defence.

open.ref: Vicsek et al. 1995, Phys. Rev. Lett. 75(6)
open.why: The minimal flocking model. A genuine order-disorder phase transition as noise falls.
Mild individual preference produces near-total segregation. Nobody wanted the outcome.
Ten thousand steps of chaos, then it builds a highway forever. Still unexplained.
Self-organised criticality with a visibly burning front.
Noise spontaneously organises into rotating spiral cores.
Phantom jams from nothing. Every driver is behaving.
Coarsening consensus with no persuasion, only copying.
One extra open site and the cluster suddenly spans the world.

open.ref: Eden 1961, Berkeley Symp. Math. Stat. Prob.
open.why: The counterpoint to DLA: same randomness, compact blob instead of filigree.

open.ref: Metropolis et al. 1953, J. Chem. Phys. 21
open.why: Magnetisation appearing at the Curie point, live.
Cooperation survives purely because it clusters. Chaotic fractal boundaries.
Mobility decides coexistence versus extinction. Spiral waves of species.
Punctuated equilibrium out of a rule with no punctuation in it.

open.ref: Olami, Feder & Christensen 1992, Phys. Rev. Lett. 68
open.why: Gutenberg-Richter law emerging from a spring-block lattice.
Similarity breeds interaction breeds similarity - and yet stable difference persists.

open.ref: Sznajd-Weron & Sznajd 2000, Int. J. Mod. Phys. C
open.why: United we stand: only pairs that agree can convince anyone.

Fluid finding the path of least resistance, trapping pockets as it goes.

open.ref: Kardar, Parisi & Zhang 1986, Phys. Rev. Lett. 56
open.why: A roughening interface whose exponents are universal.

open.ref: Gravner & Griffeath 2008, Phys. Rev. E 79; Reiter 2005
open.why: Sixfold symmetry with no template. Every one different, all six arms alike.

open.ref: Deneubourg et al. 1990, J. Insect Behav. 3
open.why: The double-bridge experiment: the colony finds the shorter path without comparing them.
Things that sync AND swarm, coupling phase to position. Five distinct states.
Real starlings track seven neighbours by rank, not by distance. Show the difference.

open.ref: Cates & Tailleur 2015, Annu. Rev. Condens. Matter Phys. 6
open.why: Purely repulsive self-propelled particles condense into a liquid. No attraction anywhere.
The chemical clock that was rejected as impossible. Target patterns and spirals.

open.model: Turing patterns on a growing domain
open.why: Angelfish stripes rearranging as the fish grows - predicted, then observed.
A memory that is nowhere in particular, recalled from a corrupted fragment.
A learned local rule that regrows a whole image after you cut it in half.

open.why: The Tokyo rail experiment itself: place the cities, let it solve the network.

Same rule, different lattice, completely different mandala.
Room VIII in two dimensions. Vastly more universes to fall into.
